experiments.hypothesis: A concrete recommended plan will reduce choice friction after free workouts are consumed.
experiments.action: At the workout limit, lead with the Athlete offer: ‘Keep training: 50 race-paced workouts for $5.99 once.’ Keep Unlimited $9.99 as the secondary comparison and show ‘No subscription’ beside both CTAs.
experiments.stop_rule: Revert if checkout-start rate is below the existing baseline after 300 views

experiments.hypothesis: Users who receive a useful first workout are more receptive to a paid plan than cold homepage visitors.
experiments.action: Below the first generated workout, add: ‘Want your next week planned too?’ Show one recommended paid option, its exact one-time price, and a ‘See Plans’ CTA. Track generated_result_upgrade_click with workout type and source.
experiments.guardrail: Workout save/print usage must not decrease
experiments.stop_rule: Remove if CTR is below 2% after 200 generated workouts

experiments.hypothesis: Users will pay when credits are framed around saved analysis and convenience, not better odds.
experiments.action: At the free-credit limit, test: ‘Continue your analysis and save your number history.’ Show Starter $3.99 and Popular $9.99, clearly labeled one-time. Do not imply that payment improves winning probability.
experiments.guardrail: No increase in gambling-responsibility complaints or misleading-claim feedback
experiments.stop_rule: Revert if verified purchase conversion declines after 300 views
